item.title: Ad Tech Briefing: Criteo named first ad tech partner to OpenAI’s ChatGPT ad pilot
item.description: Earlier this week, Criteo confirmed it is the first ad tech partner to integrate with OpenAI’s advertising pilot in the U.S., available in ChatGPT’s free and Go tiers. The move formalizes what the company first hinted at in late 2025 — that large language models would become the next frontier of its commerce media strategy. […]

item.title: OpenAI’s ad push begins, and The Knot is co-piloting
item.description: Ads have arrived in ChatGPT. The Knot is one of the first brands to try them, and is figuring out the rules as it goes.

item.title: From Boll & Branch to Bogg, brands battle a surge of AI-driven return fraud
item.description: Retailers say fraudsters are increasingly using AI tools to generate fake damage photos, receipts and documentation to claim refunds.

item.title: Agencies grapple with economics of a new marketing currency: the AI token
item.description: Token costs pose questions for under-pressure agency pricing models. Are they a line item, a cost center — or an opportunity?

item.title: WTF is Meta’s Manus tool?
item.description: Meta added a new agentic AI tool to its Ads Manager in February. Buyers have been cautiously probing its potential use cases.

item.title: Omnicom Media North America CEO Ralph Pardo on integration and disintermediation
item.description: Ralph Pardo, CEO of Omnicom Media North America, explained how far along the holding company is in absorbing IPG's agency brands, as well as why they were kept alive.

item.title: Future of TV Briefing: How Paramount’s and Warner Bros. Discovery’s ad tech stacks stack up
item.description: This week’s Future of TV Briefing breaks down Paramount’s and Warner Bros. Discovery’s ad tech stacks now that the companies seem set (finally) to combine.

item.title: Why one brand reimbursed $10,000 to customers who paid its ‘Trump Tariff Surcharge’ last year
item.description: Sexual wellness company Dame is one of the first brands to proactively return money tied to President Donald Trump’s now-invalidated tariffs.

item.title: ‘The conversation has shifted’: The CFO moved upstream. Now agencies have to as well
item.description: One interesting side effect of marketing coming under greater scrutiny in the boardroom: CFOs are working more closely with agencies than ever before.

item.title: How creator talent agencies are evolving into multi-platform operators
item.description: The legacy agency model is being re-built from the ground up to better serve the maturing creator economy – here's what that looks like.
